title: Adherence to statin therapy in childhood: comparing children's and parents' perspectives
summary: The study examines the different perceptions of treatment adherence in children with familial hypercholesterolemia. The children and one parent each are surveyed separately using a questionnaire. In addition, routinely collected laboratory parameters (e.g., LDL cholesterol) are used for comparison. The aim is to identify correlations between self-perception and external perception of therapy adherence as well as clinical target parameters. All children, adolescents, and their parents who are currently undergoing statin therapy at our lipid clinic are included. The findings will serve as a basis for family-centered interventions that improve the long-term cardiovascular prognosis of the children affected.
conditions: Children with familial hypercholesterolemia undergoing statin therapy

interventions.name: Children with familial hypercholesterolemia undergoing statin therapy aged 6-18 years with one of their primary caregivers (parents)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosed familial hypercholesterolemia or lipid metabolism disorder; Current and ongoing treatment with statins; Regular appointments at our lipid clinic; Presence of a parent or legal guardian who participates in the separate interview; Written declaration of consent (or consent of legal representatives in the case of minors)
Exclusion criteria:
Missing or incomplete written consent from minors or their legal representatives and parents; Children and adolescents who are not currently receiving statin therapy, as adherence perception is assessed in the context of ongoing therapy; Acute or serious illnesses (e.g., significant cognitive impairments or psychiatric disorders) that hinder reliable participation in the study and understanding of the questionnaires; Language barriers that prevent adequate responses to the standardized questionnaires and qualitative interviews; Parents who are not involved as primary caregivers in the daily therapy process
